sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Lower Macungie Township?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer, and the cash route usually closes soonest because no buyer's lender is waiting on an appraisal. Whichever route you pick in Lower Macungie Township, the township's building sewer inspection and the deed recording at the county Recorder of Deeds still have to happen before the keys change hands.

Lower Macungie sits in southern Lehigh County, about 7 miles southwest of Allentown. The township grew from 16,871 residents in 1990 to 30,633 in 2010, so a large share of the housing stock is relatively recent. Sellers who ask for a fast close are often handling an inherited house, a job move, a divorce, a rental with tenants, or a roof and mechanical systems that need money they would rather not spend.

  • A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, so you skip showings and listing prep.
  • You pick the closing date, which helps when a move or an estate settlement has a hard deadline.
  • The sewer inspection result, the sewer and trash certification and the transfer tax still belong in the plan, so ask who handles each one before you sign.

sections.h2: What is Lower Macungie Township like for a home seller?
sections.html:
It is a residential township of about 22.5 square miles with a mix of subdivisions, farmland and light industry. Little Lehigh Creek and Swabia Creek drain through it, South Mountain crosses the southern edge just below the boroughs of Macungie and Alburtis, and Alburtis sits entirely inside the township boundary. The Rodale Organic Gardening Experimental Farm in the township was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1999.

Students attend the East Penn School District. Ninth through twelfth graders go to Emmaus High School, middle schoolers go to Eyer Middle School or Lower Macungie Middle School, and the township has Wescosville and Willow Lane elementary schools. Buyers shopping the area often start with that district name, so it belongs in any listing or offer conversation.

Getting around is straightforward for commuters. Interstate 78 touches the extreme northern tip, PA Route 309 runs with it there, and US 222 crosses east to west. Local north to south routes include Route 100, Spring Creek Road, Willow Road and Brookside Road. Of 166.31 miles of public road, 125.26 miles are maintained by the township itself. LANta bus route 322 serves the northern tier. Police coverage has come from the Pennsylvania State Police rather than a township department.

The economy leans on manufacturing. Mack Trucks has its primary manufacturing facilities here, and Smooth-On and Allen Organ are also based in the township. Winters are cold and summers are warm and humid: the township sits in hardiness zone 6b with January averages near 29 degrees and July near 74 degrees, which is worth remembering when a buyer's inspector looks at the roof, gutters and basement.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about housing in Lower Macungie Township?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 33,507 people lived in Lower Macungie Township on July 1, 2025, up 3.3 percent from the 2020 base. Housing here is overwhelmingly owner occupied, which means most sales are a family selling the home they live in.

sections.h2: Which inspection is required before a Lower Macungie house sells?
sections.html:
The township requires a building sewer inspection before a property is sold or transferred. The inspection looks at the private sewer line that runs from the house to the township's sewer lateral, a pipe the owner, not the township, is responsible for.

  • A licensed Journeyman or Master Plumber must perform the video inspection and submit a complete Building Sewer Inspection Report, a copy of the video and proof of licensure to the township.
  • Electronic video files are not accepted. The township keeps a physical copy, preferably on a USB flash drive, in the property file for at least five years.
  • Public works staff review the submission and issue a pass or fail letter to the owner by mail, and by email if an address was supplied on the report.
  • If the line fails, the owner is responsible for the repairs before the sale. A passing result is valid for up to two years.

The township's own page lists plumbers who have supplied proof of licensure for these inspections, and you may hire a plumber who is not on that list if the plumber submits proof of licensure. The program exists because stormwater and groundwater entering private lines contribute to overflows at the Allentown wastewater plant that serves the area. The ordinance also covers transfer without inspection, so read it or call the township office at 610-966-4343 before you assume anything about timing.

sections.h2: What bills and taxes come up at a Lower Macungie closing?
sections.html:
Expect a sewer and trash certification, a sewer inspection record, and two layers of transfer tax. Each has its own office and its own lead time, so start them as soon as you have a signed agreement.

  • Sewer and trash certification: the township's utility billing office issues it for a sale or refinance for a $50 fee, and the check has to arrive before processing starts. Sewer and trash bills go out quarterly and are due within 30 days.
  • Past due utility balances: amounts more than 90 days late move to a collection law firm and stop appearing on township invoices, so clear them before closing.
  • Pennsylvania realty transfer tax: 1 percent of the value, collected by the county Recorder of Deeds, and both buyer and seller are jointly liable.
  • Local transfer tax: the township ordinance sets its share at one half of one percent, and the township and any other taxing body together may not exceed 1 percent. Ask your title company for the school district's share and who pays what under your contract.

Water is billed separately by Lehigh County Authority, so a final water reading is a separate call. Transfers between certain family members, and property passed by will or intestacy, are among the exempt categories on the state's list, which matters for inherited houses.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and assessment appeals work in Lower Macungie?
sections.html:
Lehigh County assesses at 100 percent of fair market value as of a 2013 base year, the date of its last countywide reassessment, so your assessed value is a figure from that year adjusted for new construction or demolition. The Board of Assessment Appeals accepts only an original signed appeal with the filing fee received on or before August 1 each year. Postmarks and faxed appeals do not count as timely. Interim appeals are due by the date printed on a Change of Assessment Notice.

If you are selling a rental or other property you do not live in, note that a 2026 Pennsylvania law requires non-owner-occupant owners to file contact information with the county within 30 days of buying. Owner-occupied principal residences are exempt, so the rule matters mostly to the investor who buys from you.

sections.h2: What if my Lower Macungie house needs repairs or has tenants?
sections.html:
You can still sell it, and the sewer line is the first item to sort out. Order the video inspection early, because a failed line means repair work before closing and the township mails the pass or fail letter, which takes time. If a buyer will take the house as-is, ask whether that includes sewer repairs and who pays, and put the answer in the contract.

For tenants, review the lease end date and security deposit handling with your attorney, and ask the township office about any rental rules that apply to the address. Keep copies of the sewer inspection letter, the utility certification and the deed, since the buyer's title company will ask for them.

faqs.q: Do I need an inspection to sell a house in Lower Macungie Township?
faqs.a: Yes, a building sewer video inspection by a licensed plumber is required before a sale or transfer. The township reviews it and mails a pass or fail letter, and a passing result stays valid for up to two years.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when selling in Lower Macungie?
faqs.a: The contract decides, but the law makes buyer and seller jointly liable. The state rate is 1 percent and the township's local rate is one half of one percent, with the county Recorder of Deeds collecting at recording.

faqs.q: How much is the sewer and trash certification in Lower Macungie?
faqs.a: The township charges $50 for a sewer and trash certification used for a sale or refinance. Email the utility billing office and mail the check, which must arrive before processing begins.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an assessment in Lehigh County?
faqs.a: Lehigh County takes annual appeals on or before August 1 of each year. The original signed form and filing fee must be received by then, because postmarks and faxes are not accepted.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Lower Macungie Township?
faqs.a: East Penn School District serves it. High school students go to Emmaus High School, and the township has Eyer Middle School, Lower Macungie Middle School, Wescosville Elementary and Willow Lane Elementary nearby.
